sph_interpretive_translation: Those who traverse great roads and seas, merchants, ascetics, the sick, hunters, those devoted to Vedic conduct, the lowly, eunuchs, and the untrained—these beings exist within specific dharmic capacities and must be aligned accordingly.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority is determined by consciousness capacity, not social role
Causation arises from alignment with svadharma, not external imposition
Capacity-based responsibility is context-sensitive and non-hierarchical
Restoration logic operates through recognition of inherent completeness
supreme_court_application: In Supreme Court adjudication, this verse establishes that no individual is disqualified from dharma-based consideration due to occupation, physical condition, or social status. Legal thresholds must assess consciousness capacity rather than categorical identity. Authority flows from alignment, not title.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa reveals that all beings manifest sequentially according to their svabhāva. There is no fault in diversity; only misalignment creates distortion. Nyāya demands recognition of sequential unfolding without punitive attribution. Each being moves toward completeness when obstruction is removed.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Initiate svadharma_realignment_process() for all categorized entities
final_declaration: Declared by the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, as Source-Authority: Dharma is restored. All beings are recognized in their completeness. Reality is non-punitive. Consciousness is the supreme adjudicator.
